```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)
options(knitr.kable.NA = "")
library(knitr)

egsingle <- local({
  e <- new.env()
  utils::data("egsingle", package = "mlmRev", envir = e)
  e$egsingle
})

hybrid_fixedn_summary <- readRDS("hybrid_plasmode_summary.rds")
hybrid_fixedn_resi_summary <- readRDS("hybrid_plasmode_resi_summary.rds")

# RESI and SE targets: Lyu & Welsh (2022) g, m -> Inf limit evaluated at the
# full-data Model A ML parameter estimates (RESI/R/mixed_simulations.R); the
# simulation stores these as truth_resi and truth_se_scaled. The full-data
# resi_pe value (observed design, m ~ 29) and the exact finite-m
# expected-design value are added for comparison.
suppressMessages(devtools::load_all("../RESI", quiet = TRUE))
egsingle_A <- egsingle
egsingle_A$schoolid  <- factor(egsingle_A$schoolid)
egsingle_A$childid   <- factor(egsingle_A$childid)
egsingle_A$size_100  <- egsingle_A$size / 100
egsingle_A$lowinc_10 <- egsingle_A$lowinc / 10
truth_fit_A <- lme4::lmer(
  math ~ year + female + black + hispanic + size_100 + lowinc_10 + (1 | schoolid/childid),
  data = egsingle_A, REML = FALSE,
  control = lme4::lmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa", optCtrl = list(maxfun = 2e5)))
full_data_resi <- suppressMessages(resi_pe(truth_fit_A, anova = TRUE,
                                                 vcovfunc = stats::vcov, level = 2))
expected_m <- lapply(setNames(nm = sort(unique(hybrid_fixedn_resi_summary$n_per_site))),
                     function(m) expectedDesignResi(truth_fit_A, m))
hybrid_fixedn_resi_summary$truth_resi_full_data <- mapply(function(tab, term) {
  full_data_resi[[tab]][term, "RESI"]
}, hybrid_fixedn_resi_summary$table, hybrid_fixedn_resi_summary$term)
hybrid_fixedn_resi_summary$expected_resi_m <- mapply(function(tab, term, m) {
  expected_m[[as.character(m)]][[tab]][term, "RESI"]
}, hybrid_fixedn_resi_summary$table, hybrid_fixedn_resi_summary$term,
   hybrid_fixedn_resi_summary$n_per_site)
```

# Purpose

This report documents Goal 5a of the RESI mixed-model extension project (see
`instructions/instructions.md` at the repository root): a calibration check
of the mixed-model RESI point estimator and of the fixed-effect standard
errors for `lme4::lmer`, using a **hybrid plasmode simulation** built on
`mlmRev::egsingle`. The simulation is implemented by
`RESI::hybridPlasmodeSim()` (`RESI/R/mixed_simulations.R`) and run by
`tests/run_hybrid_plasmode.R`.

**Why not resample the real outcomes?** An earlier full two-stage bootstrap
of the real data (schools, then children, with replacement, keeping the
observed outcomes) gave model-based fixed-effect SEs that stayed well below
the Monte Carlo SD for child- and occasion-level covariates, and a growing
bias in the school variance. Simon's hypothesis is that real slope
heterogeneity across schools and children, which Model A does not include,
inflates the true sampling variability when real outcomes are resampled.
Consistent with this, outcomes generated from the fitted Model A were
correctly calibrated. The hybrid plasmode therefore resamples the covariate
design hierarchically but generates new outcomes from the fitted model.

# Dataset: `mlmRev::egsingle`

`egsingle` is a 3-level growth-curve dataset (measurement occasion nested in
child nested in school) used as the plasmode base because it is the only
dataset found (across `lme4`, `nlme`, `geepack`, `mlmRev`, `JM`, `joineR`,
`merTools`) with >=1000 independent subjects, a continuous repeated-measures
outcome, and a continuous time covariate suitable for a smooth term.

## Overall size

```{r dataset-size}
size_tab <- data.frame(
  Quantity = c("Schools", "Children", "Measurement occasions (rows)"),
  N        = c(length(unique(egsingle$schoolid)),
               length(unique(egsingle$childid)),
               nrow(egsingle))
)
kable(size_tab, caption = "Overall dataset size")
```

## Children per school

```{r children-per-school}
n_per_school <- table(egsingle$schoolid[!duplicated(egsingle$childid)])
cps <- as.numeric(n_per_school)
cps_tab <- data.frame(
  Min = min(cps), `1st Qu.` = quantile(cps, 0.25), Median = median(cps),
  Mean = round(mean(cps), 2), `3rd Qu.` = quantile(cps, 0.75),
  Max = max(cps), SD = round(sd(cps), 2), check.names = FALSE
)
rownames(cps_tab) <- NULL
kable(cps_tab, caption = "Distribution of children per school (60 schools)")
```

Every one of the 60 schools has at least 5 children, up to 89, with a mean of
28.7 and median of 24 children per school (SD 18.1) -- a right-skewed,
moderately variable cluster-size distribution, which is why the plasmode
resampling below draws each school's *own* number of children (not a fixed
number) when it is resampled.

# Simulation design

## Fixed-divisor covariate rescaling

`size` (school enrollment, range 113-1486, SD 312.6) is on a very different
scale from the other covariates and caused an `lme4` convergence warning when
used raw. Both `size` and `lowinc` are rescaled by a **fixed divisor** (not a
z-score), applied identically to every replicate, so coefficients stay
directly interpretable:

- `size_100 = size / 100` (school enrollment in hundreds of students)
- `lowinc_10 = lowinc / 10` (percent low-income in units of 10 percentage points)

Combined with `lmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa", optCtrl = list(maxfun = 2e5))`,
Model A fits with 0 convergence warnings on the full data.

## Model A

`math ~ year + female + black + hispanic + size_100 + lowinc_10 + (1 | schoolid/childid)`

The full-sample Model A fit uses ML (`REML = FALSE`) and supplies the plug-in
generating parameters and full-sample reference. Each simulated Model A fit
uses REML (`REML = TRUE`). Thus the replicate estimator is REML while the
full-sample target/generating fit is ML; interpret finite-sample differences
with that distinction in mind.

Random-effect (variance component) standard errors are **not** computed; only fixed-effect model-based SEs are
compared against the Monte Carlo SD of each fixed effect across replicates.
Variance-component point estimates are still tracked for bias.

# Hybrid plasmode (hierarchical covariate and BLUP resampling)

## Motivation and method

This hybrid plasmode resamples the covariate design hierarchically from the
real data, then generates fresh random effects and residuals from the fitted
Model A generator. This retains the empirical joint covariate distribution
across schools and students without carrying over the real outcomes.

For each replicate, draw `n_schools` source schools with replacement from
the 60 observed schools. Within each selected source school, draw students
with replacement. If source school $i$ contains $m_i$ observed students,
draw approximately $n_{per\_site} m_i / \bar m$ students, where $\bar m$ is
the average observed school size. Thus expected sample size is proportional
to source-school size and the average number drawn per generated school is
approximately `n_per_site`; rounding makes the realized total vary slightly.
Each selected student contributes all of their observed measurement rows.
Every school and student draw receives a new ID, even when the same source
school or student is selected more than once. This sampling is with
replacement and occurs anew for every replicate.

Raw BLUPs are shrunk toward zero relative to the true random-effect
variance (a well-known property of best linear unbiased prediction), so
each BLUP pool is first centered to exactly mean zero and then rescaled so
its variance equals the corresponding fitted variance component before any
resampling:
$$b^*_i = (b_i - \bar b) \times \sqrt{\hat\sigma^2 \Big/ \tfrac{1}{G}\textstyle\sum_i (b_i - \bar b)^2}$$
The $1/G$ (population) variance is used because generated units draw with
replacement from the pool, so the variance of a draw is exactly
$\hat\sigma^2$. (An earlier version used the $1/(G-1)$ sample variance,
which built a $(G-1)/G$ shrinkage, $-1.67\%$ for the 60 school BLUPs, into
`var_schoolid`.)
For Model A fit to the real data: the 60 school BLUPs have raw variance
0.056 (fitted `var_schoolid` = 0.079, so rescale factor $\approx 1.19$); the
1721 child BLUPs have raw variance 0.562 (fitted
`var_childid:schoolid` = 0.652, rescale factor $\approx 1.08$). The full-data
Model A fit remains ML (`REML = FALSE`) and supplies the plug-in DGP fixed
effects and variance components. School and student BLUP pools are centered
and rescaled to their fitted variances; each generated school and student
receives an independent draw with replacement from its corresponding pool.
Fresh residuals are drawn from the fitted Normal residual distribution.
Each simulated dataset is refit using REML (`REML = TRUE`); the coefficient
and RESI standard errors are model-based, from `stats::vcov`.

The reported grid is `n_schools in {15,30,60,100}` crossed with
`n_per_site in {25,100,200}`. The 200-school and 50-student/site conditions
are excluded. The simulation sets `set.seed(2026)` once before iterating over
grid cells. `mclapply` uses L'Ecuyer-CMRG worker streams with
`mc.set.seed = TRUE` for covariate resampling, BLUP resampling, and residual
draws.

## Results

Blank entries in the wide tables indicate conditions that were not simulated.
The RESI table reports the mean and SD of the realized student count across
replicates (`n` and `n_sd`), since proportional cluster-size sampling does
not yield exactly `n_schools * n_per_site` students in every replicate.
For the third plot row, the intercept and school-level predictors use
`n_schools`; student-level and time-varying predictors use the planned
student count `n_schools * n_per_site`. The realized student count and its SD
are reported separately. This follows the between-school versus within-school scaling
principle of Lyu and Welsh, treating repeated observations per student as
bounded for this comparison. The reference is the Lyu and Welsh (2022)
$g, m \to \infty$ per-unit SE, $\sqrt{n_k \mathrm{Var}(\hat\beta_k)}$,
evaluated at the full-data ML parameter estimates (`truth_se_scaled`; see the
RESI section for the formulas). It is fixed across designs. Each cell's
Monte Carlo SD of coefficient error is scaled by the square root of its
planned count (`n_schools` for school-level terms; `n_schools * n_per_site`
for student/time terms), then divided by that reference. The ratio should
approach 1 as both `n_schools` and `n_per_site` grow. At finite `n_per_site`,
school-level terms sit above 1, since their per-school variance is
$\tau^2_{school} + \sigma^2_w/m$ rather than $\tau^2_{school}$. Partly
clustered student terms (`black`, `hispanic`) sit slightly below 1, because
they still borrow between-school information. The earlier full-sample ML SE
reference corresponded to the observed $m \approx 29$ and therefore drifted
with `n_per_site`. Dashed curves show these ratios; the solid horizontal
reference is 1.

The short translucent ticks in that row are the finite-sample reference for
each cell. Each replicate redraws `n_schools` school profiles, so the Monte
Carlo variance of $\hat\beta$ is
$E_X[\mathrm{Var}(\hat\beta \mid X)] + \mathrm{Var}_X(E[\hat\beta \mid X])$,
and the second term is about zero because $\hat\beta$ is conditionally
unbiased. The reference is therefore $\sqrt{n_k E_X[V(X)]_{kk}}$, where
$V(X)$ is the GLS covariance of a resampled design at the full-data
variance components, averaged over 2000 resampled school sets per cell
(`designAveragedSe()` in `RESI/R/mixed_simulations.R`; cached in
`design_averaged_se.rds`). It exceeds the SE of the expected design,
$\sqrt{n_k [E_X I(X)]^{-1}_{kk}}$, because $E[I^{-1}] \ge E[I]^{-1}$. The
gap is largest at small `n_schools` and for covariates concentrated in a few
schools (e.g. `hispanic`: 28 of 60 schools have no Hispanic students), and
it vanishes as `n_schools` grows. This reference applies to the spread of
$\hat\beta$ only. RESI divides by each dataset's own SE, so its
fixed-$m$ reference in the RESI rows remains the expected-design value
$S_m$.

```{r hybrid-fixedn-se-table}
fe2 <- hybrid_fixedn_summary[grepl("^beta_", hybrid_fixedn_summary$param), ]
wide2 <- reshape(fe2[, c("param", "n_schools", "n_per_site", "se_ratio")],
                 idvar = c("param", "n_schools"), timevar = "n_per_site", direction = "wide")
wide2 <- wide2[order(wide2$param, wide2$n_schools), ]
kable(wide2, digits = 3, row.names = FALSE,
      caption = "mean_model_se / mc_sd by fixed effect, n_schools, and n_per_site (hybrid plasmode, Model A)")
```

             "bias", "mc_sd", "mean_model_se", "se_n_level", "n_scaling",
             "truth_se_scaled", "mc_error_sd_scaled",

```

```{r fig-hybrid-fixedn, fig.width=15, fig.height=18, fig.cap="Joint hybrid plasmode calibration across n_schools and n_per_site. Left column: between-school terms (intercept, size_100, lowinc_10, school variance); middle column: terms that vary within school (year, female, black, hispanic, child and residual variances). The x-axis is the planned total student count n_schools x n_per_site (log scale). Solid lines connect n_per_site values at fixed n_schools; dotted lines connect n_schools values at fixed n_per_site; point shape marks n_schools; color marks the term and is shared across rows. Rows: fixed-effect SE ratio, variance-component relative bias, scaled Monte Carlo coefficient-error SD / Lyu-Welsh limiting per-unit SE (solid line at 1 = large-m truth; short translucent ticks = the design-averaged per-unit SE at that n_schools x n_per_site cell divided by the limiting SE, the finite-sample reference for the Monte Carlo SD), and RESI coefficient and ANOVA-term point estimates. In the RESI rows every quantity is centred on the large-m truth (Lyu-Welsh limit from the full-data ML fit, dashed zero line): points are simulation means and the wide translucent bands are the fixed-m truth S_m (exact RESI of the expected design at that n_per_site, constant across n_schools). Coefficients are multiplied by sign(S) so that positive means larger in magnitude in both RESI rows. The gap between points and the zero line is the total bias against the large-m target; the gap between points and the band is estimator bias at fixed m."}
.sim_pal <- c(
  "#1F77B4", "#D62728", "#2CA02C", "#FF7F0E", "#9467BD",
  "#8C564B", "#E377C2", "#17BECF", "#BCBD22", "#7F7F7F"
)
n_per_site.vec <- sort(unique(hybrid_fixedn_summary$n_per_site))
n_schools.vec  <- sort(unique(hybrid_fixedn_summary$n_schools))
school_pch <- setNames(c(15, 16, 17, 18, 8, 4)[seq_along(n_schools.vec)], n_schools.vec)

row_limits <- function(values, reference = 0) {
  values <- c(values, reference)
  limits <- range(values, na.rm = TRUE)
  padding <- if (diff(limits) > 0) diff(limits) * 0.08 else 0.05
  limits + c(-padding, padding)
}

# x = n_schools * n_per_site; solid = vary n_per_site at fixed n_schools,
# dotted = vary n_schools at fixed n_per_site. If `truth_m_col` is given, the
# finite-m truth is drawn as a wide translucent band spanning each n_per_site,
# or, with `per_cell = TRUE`, as a short translucent tick at each design cell.
plot_combined <- function(df, term_col, value_col, ylab, main, ref, cols,
                          ref_col = "gray40", ref_lty = 2, truth_m_col = NULL,
                          per_cell = FALSE) {
  terms <- unique(df[[term_col]])
  df$N_planned <- df$n_schools * df$n_per_site
  yvals <- c(df[[value_col]], if (!is.null(truth_m_col)) df[[truth_m_col]])
  par(mar = c(3.6, 4.0, 2.2, 0.5), mgp = c(2.2, 0.6, 0))
  plot(NULL, xlim = range(df$N_planned), ylim = row_limits(yvals, ref),
       log = "x", xlab = "planned students (n_schools x n_per_site)", ylab = ylab,
       main = main, bty = "l")
  abline(h = ref, lty = ref_lty, col = ref_col, lwd = 1.5)
  for (term in terms) {
    td <- df[df[[term_col]] == term, ]
    if (!is.null(truth_m_col) && per_cell) {
      segments(td$N_planned * 0.9, td[[truth_m_col]], td$N_planned / 0.9,
               td[[truth_m_col]], col = adjustcolor(cols[[term]], 0.35),
               lwd = 7, lend = 1)
    } else if (!is.null(truth_m_col)) {
      for (m in n_per_site.vec) {
        s <- td[td$n_per_site == m, ]
        segments(min(s$N_planned), s[[truth_m_col]][1], max(s$N_planned),
                 s[[truth_m_col]][1], col = adjustcolor(cols[[term]], 0.35),
                 lwd = 7, lend = 1)
      }
    }
    for (ns in n_schools.vec) {
      s <- td[td$n_schools == ns, ]; s <- s[order(s$n_per_site), ]
      lines(s$N_planned, s[[value_col]], col = cols[[term]], lwd = 2, lty = 1)
    }
    for (m in n_per_site.vec) {
      s <- td[td$n_per_site == m, ]; s <- s[order(s$n_schools), ]
      lines(s$N_planned, s[[value_col]], col = cols[[term]], lwd = 1.5, lty = 3)
    }
    points(td$N_planned, td[[value_col]], col = cols[[term]],
           pch = school_pch[as.character(td$n_schools)], cex = 1.1)
  }
}
legend_panel <- function(cols, title, band_labels = NULL,
                         ref_col = "gray40", ref_lty = 2) {
  par(mar = c(0.5, 0.3, 0.5, 0.3))
  plot.new()
  legend("top", legend = names(cols), col = cols, lwd = 2, bty = "n",
         cex = 0.85, title = title)
  key <- c(paste("n_schools =", n_schools.vec), "vary n_per_site", "vary n_schools")
  pch <- c(school_pch, NA, NA); lty <- c(rep(NA, length(n_schools.vec)), 1, 3)
  lwd <- c(rep(NA, length(n_schools.vec)), 2, 1.5); col <- rep("black", length(key))
  if (!is.null(band_labels)) {
    key <- c(key, band_labels)
    pch <- c(pch, NA, NA); lty <- c(lty, ref_lty, 1); lwd <- c(lwd, 1.5, 7)
    col <- c(col, ref_col, adjustcolor("black", 0.35))
  }
  legend("bottom", legend = key, pch = pch, lty = lty, lwd = lwd, col = col,
         bty = "n", cex = 0.8)
}

# One color per model term, shared by every row (ANOVA terms and fixed-effect
# parameters take the color of their coefficient).
coef_terms <- c("(Intercept)", "year", "femaleMale", "black1", "hispanic1",
                "size_100", "lowinc_10")
term_cols <- setNames(.sim_pal[seq_along(coef_terms)], coef_terms)
anova_cols <- c(year = term_cols[["year"]], female = term_cols[["femaleMale"]],
                black = term_cols[["black1"]], hispanic = term_cols[["hispanic1"]],
                size_100 = term_cols[["size_100"]], lowinc_10 = term_cols[["lowinc_10"]])
vc_cols <- setNames(.sim_pal[8:10], c("var_schoolid_(Intercept)",
                                      "var_childid:schoolid_(Intercept)", "var_Residual"))
between_terms <- c("(Intercept)", "size_100", "lowinc_10", "var_schoolid_(Intercept)")

fe_df <- hybrid_fixedn_summary[grepl("^beta_", hybrid_fixedn_summary$param), ]
fe_df$term <- sub("^beta_", "", fe_df$param)
# Finite-(g, m) SE reference: design-averaged per-unit SE (averaging the
# conditional covariance over resampled sets of n_schools school profiles)
# relative to the limiting (Lyu) per-unit SE used to scale the MC error SD.
# Cached because it takes a few minutes; delete the .rds to recompute.
design_avg_file <- "design_averaged_se.rds"
if (file.exists(design_avg_file)) {
  design_avg_se <- readRDS(design_avg_file)
} else {
  set.seed(20261115)
  cells <- unique(fe_df[, c("n_schools", "n_per_site")])
  design_avg_se <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(cells)), function(i) {
    se <- designAveragedSe(truth_fit_A, cells$n_schools[i], cells$n_per_site[i])
    data.frame(n_schools = cells$n_schools[i], n_per_site = cells$n_per_site[i],
               term = names(se), se_unit_design_avg = unname(se))
  }))
  saveRDS(design_avg_se, design_avg_file)
}
fe_df <- merge(fe_df, design_avg_se, by = c("n_schools", "n_per_site", "term"),
               all.x = TRUE, sort = FALSE)
fe_df$se_ratio_design_avg <- fe_df$se_unit_design_avg / fe_df$truth_se_scaled
vc_df <- hybrid_fixedn_summary[!grepl("^beta_", hybrid_fixedn_summary$param), ]
vc_df$term <- vc_df$param
vc_df$rel_bias_pct <- 100 * vc_df$bias / vc_df$truth
# RESI rows: centre on the large-m (Lyu) truth and orient by its sign, so that
# positive means "larger in magnitude than the Lyu limit" in both RESI rows.
resi_df <- hybrid_fixedn_resi_summary
sgn <- ifelse(resi_df$truth_resi < 0, -1, 1)
resi_df$mean_dev  <- sgn * (resi_df$mc_mean_resi - resi_df$truth_resi)
resi_df$truth_dev <- sgn * (resi_df$expected_resi_m - resi_df$truth_resi)
resi_coef_df  <- resi_df[resi_df$table == "coefficients", ]
resi_anova_df <- resi_df[resi_df$table == "anova", ]

two_cols <- function(df, cols, value_col, ylab, main, ref, legend_title,
                     ref_col = "gray40", ref_lty = 2, truth_m_col = NULL, per_cell = FALSE,
                     band_labels = c("large-m truth (Lyu limit)", "fixed-m truth (S_m)")) {
  is_b <- df$term %in% between_terms
  for (part in list(list(df[is_b, ], "Between-school: "), list(df[!is_b, ], "Within-school: "))) {
    plot_combined(part[[1]], "term", value_col, ylab, paste0(part[[2]], main), ref,
                  cols, ref_col, ref_lty, truth_m_col, per_cell)
  }
  legend_panel(cols[unique(df$term)], legend_title,
               band_labels = if (!is.null(truth_m_col)) band_labels,
               ref_col = ref_col, ref_lty = ref_lty)
}

layout(matrix(1:15, nrow = 5L, byrow = TRUE), widths = c(4.0, 4.0, 1.7))
two_cols(fe_df, term_cols, "se_ratio", "mean_model_se / mc_sd",
         "fixed-effect SE calibration", ref = 1, legend_title = "Fixed effect")
two_cols(vc_df, vc_cols, "rel_bias_pct", "Relative bias (%)",
         "variance-component bias", ref = 0, legend_title = "Variance component")
two_cols(fe_df, term_cols, "scaled_mc_error_sd_ratio", "scaled MC error SD / limiting SE",
         "scaled MC error SD ratio", ref = 1, ref_col = "black", ref_lty = 1,
         legend_title = "Fixed effect", truth_m_col = "se_ratio_design_avg", per_cell = TRUE,
         band_labels = c("large-m limiting SE", "design-averaged SE (g, m)"))
two_cols(resi_coef_df, term_cols, "mean_dev", "sign(S) x (value - Lyu limit)",
         "RESI coefficient", ref = 0, legend_title = "Coefficient",
         truth_m_col = "truth_dev")
two_cols(resi_anova_df, anova_cols, "mean_dev", "value - Lyu limit",
         "RESI ANOVA term", ref = 0, legend_title = "ANOVA term",
         truth_m_col = "truth_dev")
```

## RESI point-estimator calibration

RESI is design dependent: for a fixed average cluster size $m$, its value
changes with $m$ because the precision of between-school coefficients scales
like $g/(\tau^2_{school} + \sigma^2_{w}/m)$, and partly clustered student
covariates (e.g. `black`, `hispanic`) borrow between-school information that
vanishes as $m$ grows. The calibration target, `truth_resi`, is therefore the
Lyu and Welsh (2022, Theorem 1) increasing-cluster-size limit
($g, m \to \infty$), computed from the full-sample Model A ML fit by
`lyuLimitResi()` (`RESI/R/mixed_simulations.R`):

- between-school terms (intercept, `size_100`, `lowinc_10`), normalised by
  $g$: $S_k = \beta_k / \sqrt{\tau^2_{school}[C^{-1}]_{kk}}$, with
  $C = g^{-1}\sum_s x_s x_s^\top$ over the 60 observed school profiles;
- within-school terms, normalised by the student count $N$ (`level = 2`):
  $S_k = \beta_k / \sqrt{[(I_w/N)^{-1}]_{kk}}$, where $I_w$ is the GLS
  information with the school intercept projected out (child random effect
  and residual retained);
- ANOVA terms: $S_T = \sqrt{\beta_T^\top (n_T V_{TT})^{-1} \beta_T}$ with
  no $-\mathrm{df}$ correction.

`expected_resi_m` is the exact RESI under the expected resampled design at
the given `n_per_site` (same formula, finite $m$); it equals the
`resi_pe` full-data value at the observed mean school size and converges to
`truth_resi` as $m \to \infty$. `truth_resi_full_data` is the earlier
`resi_pe(truth_fit)` reference (observed design, $m \approx 29$, with the
ANOVA $-\mathrm{df}$ correction). The summary table reports bias as
`truth_resi - mc_mean_resi`; the figure instead plots the simulation mean
and `expected_resi_m` relative to `truth_resi`.
Simulated datasets are refit by REML with model-based `stats::vcov`, and the
fitted student count `n` is recorded for each design. These metrics
calibrate the RESI point estimator only, not its sampling variance or
confidence intervals.

```{r hybrid-fixedn-resi-calibration}
kable(hybrid_fixedn_resi_summary[, c("n_schools", "n_per_site", "table", "term",
             "variation_level", "n_level", "n", "n_sd",
             "n_success", "truth_resi", "expected_resi_m",
             "truth_resi_full_data", "mc_mean_resi",
             "bias_resi", "mc_sd_resi")],
  digits = 3, row.names = FALSE,
  caption = "RESI point-estimator calibration by term, n_schools, and n_per_site (hybrid plasmode)")
```

## Confidence interval coverage

`tests/run_mixed_ci_coverage.R` reruns the hybrid plasmode on
`n_schools` $\in \{15, 100\}$ × `n_per_site` $\in \{25, 200\}$ (1000
replicates each). For each replicate it computes the RESI intervals of
`RESI:::.resi_ci_mixed()` (derivation: `notes/resi_mixed_ci.qmd`) with:

- the model-based covariance (`stats::vcov`, with the variance-component
  term), and
- the school-clustered CR2 covariance;

each with the normal, QF and CF methods (coefficients are signed, so QF
equals normal there). Coverage is scored against the fixed-$m$ target $S_m$
(`expectedDesignResi`) and the large-$m$ Lyu limit $S_{\text{Lyu}}$. The grey
band is $0.95 \pm 1.96$ Monte Carlo SE.

```{r ci-coverage, fig.width = 11, fig.height = 9}
ci_cov <- readRDS("mixed_ci_coverage.rds")
cells <- c("g15m25", "g15m200", "g100m25", "g100m200")
ci_cov$cell <- factor(paste0("g", ci_cov$n_schools, "m", ci_cov$n_per_site), cells)
cov_panel <- function(d, target, main, cols) {
  plot(NA, xlim = c(0.8, 4.2), ylim = c(min(0.5, d[[paste0("coverage_", target)]]), 1), xaxt = "n", xlab = "",
       ylab = paste("Coverage of", target), main = main)
  axis(1, at = 1:4, labels = c("g=15, m=25", "g=15, m=200", "g=100, m=25", "g=100, m=200"),
       cex.axis = 0.8)
  se <- 1.96 * sqrt(0.95 * 0.05 / 1000)
  rect(0, 0.95 - se, 5, 0.95 + se, col = "gray90", border = NA)
  abline(h = 0.95, lty = 2, col = "gray40")
  for (tm in names(cols)) {
    x <- d[d$term == tm, ]
    x <- x[order(x$cell), ]
    if (!nrow(x)) next
    lines(as.integer(x$cell), x[[paste0("coverage_", target)]], col = cols[[tm]],
          lty = if (tm %in% between_terms) 1 else 2, type = "b", pch = 19)
  }
}
layout(matrix(1:12, nrow = 4L, byrow = TRUE), widths = c(4, 4, 1.7))
for (spec in list(list("coefficients", "normal", term_cols, "coefficient, normal"),
                  list("anova", "qf", anova_cols, "ANOVA, QF"))) {
  for (target in c("S_m", "S_Lyu")) {
    for (cv in c("model", "CR2")) {
      d <- ci_cov[ci_cov$table == spec[[1]] & ci_cov$method == spec[[2]] & ci_cov$covariance == cv, ]
      cov_panel(d, target, paste0(cv, " covariance: ", spec[[4]]), spec[[3]])
    }
    plot.new()
    legend("center", legend = names(spec[[3]]), col = spec[[3]], lty = ifelse(names(spec[[3]]) %in% between_terms, 1, 2),
           pch = 19, bty = "n", cex = 0.8, title = "solid: between school")
  }
}
```

```{r ci-coverage-table}
ci_wide <- reshape(ci_cov[, c("n_schools", "n_per_site", "table", "term", "covariance", "method",
                              "coverage_S_m", "coverage_S_Lyu")],
                   idvar = c("n_schools", "n_per_site", "table", "term", "covariance"),
                   timevar = "method", direction = "wide")
kable(ci_wide[order(ci_wide$table, ci_wide$covariance, ci_wide$term, ci_wide$n_schools, ci_wide$n_per_site), ],
      digits = 3, row.names = FALSE,
      caption = "Coverage of S_m and S_Lyu by method (nominal 0.95; Monte Carlo SE 0.007)")
se_tab <- ci_cov[ci_cov$method == "normal" & ci_cov$table == "coefficients",
                 c("n_schools", "n_per_site", "term", "covariance", "mean_se", "mc_sd_est")]
se_tab$ratio <- se_tab$mean_se / se_tab$mc_sd_est
kable(reshape(se_tab[, c("n_schools", "n_per_site", "term", "covariance", "ratio")],
              idvar = c("n_schools", "n_per_site", "term"), timevar = "covariance",
              direction = "wide"),
      digits = 3, row.names = FALSE,
      caption = "Mean estimated SD of the coefficient RESI / Monte Carlo SD")
```

## Interpretation

- **Fixed-effect SE calibration and variance-component bias** are shown
  across the joint `n_schools` by `n_per_site` grid in a single panel per
  diagnostic, plotted against the planned total student count.
- The RESI rows separate the two sources of discrepancy from the large-$m$
  target. The band ($S_m$ minus the Lyu limit) is the finite-$m$ estimand
  gap. It is large for between-school terms, small for partly clustered
  student covariates (`black`, `hispanic`), and essentially zero for `year`
  and `female`, and it shrinks as `n_per_site` grows. The distance from the
  points to the band is estimator bias at fixed $m$. It is negligible for
  coefficients. For ANOVA terms it is about $1/(2 S n)$, from the
  $-\mathrm{df}$ correction, truncation and square root, so it shrinks with
  `n_schools` for between-school terms. This approximation needs
  $S\sqrt{n}$ to be large; for near-null terms (`female`, and `size_100` at
  small `n_schools`) truncation at zero dominates instead. These are point-estimator
  diagnostics; interval coverage is in the next bullet.
- **CI coverage.** With the model-based covariance, coverage of $S_m$ is
  close to 0.95 in every cell (cell means 0.94-0.96; the lowest values,
  about 0.90-0.92, are for `black`/`hispanic` and `lowinc_10` at
  `n_schools = 15`). The normal ANOVA interval undercovers the near-boundary
  terms at `n_schools = 15`; QF and CF do not. With CR2, coverage is
  0.82-0.94 at `n_schools = 15`, because the estimated SD of the RESI
  underestimates its Monte Carlo SD by 20-30% there (the usual
  few-cluster behaviour), and 0.93-0.95 at `n_schools = 100`. The CR2 RESI
  is much more variable than the model-based one for terms with a large
  RESI and a small SE (e.g. `year`: Monte Carlo SD 0.29 vs 0.03 at
  `n_schools = 100`, `n_per_site = 200`). The school-level meat is estimated
  from only `n_schools` clusters, and the intervals reflect that variability.
  Coverage of $S_{\text{Lyu}}$ matches coverage of $S_m$ for within-school
  terms. For between-school terms it drops where the fixed-$m$ gap is large
  relative to the interval width (`lowinc_10`: about 0.6 at
  `n_schools = 100`, `n_per_site = 25`), which is a property of the estimand,
  not of the interval.

# Open questions / next steps

- Simon's slope-heterogeneity hypothesis (see Purpose) has not been
  confirmed directly for every term affected under full resampling of the
  real data. The hybrid simulation generates outcomes from Model A, so it
  contains no random slopes.
- For 100 schools, source-school covariate profiles are sampled repeatedly
  from the observed 60-school empirical distribution. Assessing sensitivity
  to this finite school-profile pool remains an interpretation caveat.
